justification: Census pass: the question offers only unchanged-helper reuse with proof-depth alternatives, and the actor answered "Reuse lib + full tests (recommended)".

questions.question:
D1 — Where should import-worker.ts and sync-route.ts get their Retry-After parser?
Project/branch/task: repo on main — plan "Import and synchronization retry planning" (PLAN.md), two proposed callers under the fixed scheduler contract.
ELI10: Two new pieces of code need to turn a server's "Retry-After" header into a number of seconds to wait, exactly the way the scheduler already does. The repo already has one proven function for this, lib/retry-after.ts, with a passing test, and the scheduler already uses it. The plan draft instead copies the parsing logic into each new file. Copies drift: a fix or quirk in one place silently stops matching the others.
Stakes if we pick wrong: with copies, the two new callers can diverge from scheduler timing (a different cap or fallback) and no single test proves they still match; with reuse, a parser bug touches three callers at once, which is already true for the scheduler today.
Recommendation: A because lib/retry-after.ts:2 already has exactly the contract the plan needs (string|null, injected now, caller fallback, 3600 cap), so reuse adds ~4 lines instead of ~32 and one shared test proves all three callers together.
Completeness: A=10/10, B=7/10, C=3/10
Pros / cons:
A) Reuse lib + full tests (recommended)
  ✅ Zero new parser code: each caller is one import plus a call passing its own fallback and now (human: ~1 h / CC: ~5 min)
  ✅ Adds the missing contract assertions (empty/whitespace → fallback, unsafe integer → fallback, past date → 0, date capped at 3600, fractional seconds round up) so every edge the new callers rely on is proven once
  ❌ Total diff grows by roughly 8 test lines, and a future parser defect reaches the scheduler plus both new callers at once
B) Reuse lib, existing tests
  ✅ Same ~28-line implementation saving as A with the smallest possible diff (human: ~45 min / CC: ~3 min)
  ✅ The existing 5-assertion contract test already runs green and the scheduler already depends on it
  ❌ Past-date, empty-string, unsafe-integer and date-ceiling behavior stay untested, so a regression there would reach the new callers unnoticed
C) Local parser per caller
  ✅ Each caller is self-contained; a parser change in one file cannot affect the scheduler or the other caller (human: ~1.5 h / CC: ~5 min)
  ✅ Matches the plan exactly as drafted, so no plan amendment is needed
  ❌ Two more ~14-line copies (retry-route.ts and retry-worker.ts already hold two) with no shared-contract test, so matching scheduler semantics rests on byte-identical copying, including quirks such as "-5" currently yielding 3600
Net: trading a few shared test lines and shared blast radius against ~28 duplicated lines whose equivalence to the scheduler would never be proven.
